I'm curious after this AshleyMadison leak was posted to the "dark Internet"...

The "darknet" is a section of the internet that can't be accessed by conventional means (google, etc.). Websites on it are hosted on .onion extensions. It can be home to a variety of content, much like the "clearnet", which is what you're on now, but it's mainly recognized for hosting illegal content (drugs, CP, dox info, etc.) Tor can be used to safely browse it anonymously, but you need to be extremely careful if you want to get into the illegal stuff.

Web sites, or sites using protocols, "on top of" the internet, so a person "on the dark net" cannot be identified or traced. Usually.

Sometimes the person's IP is changed by a proxy, sometimes all data is encrypted that runs from site to site. http://www.freenetproject.org is software to set up file sharing over encrypted connections, but parts of the files are scatted over dozens of computers. There is no central computer or central person to arrest.
